evidence: Workbook Quality Checks #35 (row 36): 'At least one criterion proves the product's defining behavior works, and (where stateful) that state survives a reload / re-auth and is server-backed where required.' Skill quality-checks.md s.35 says the same. (1) Defining behaviour is graded: tests/scored/functional/judge.toml grades the board (hro_move_one_stage w1.5, hro_reorder w1.5, hro_bulk_move w1.5, hro_bulk_all_or_none w2, hro_undo_restores w2, hro_undo_conflict w2, hro_stale_refused w2, hro_live_board w2) and conversations (hro_msg_exchange, hro_thread_latest/earlier, hro_unread_counts, hro_seen, hro_drafts), matching the two pillars of instruction.md. (2) Server-backed: constraints gate hro_gate_shared adds a card through the UI, reloads (still signed in, card still there), and reads it as the Observer in 'a new independent empty browser context' ('a browser-only save does not satisfy the gate'); the same check is the global gate in functional prompt.md:11 and the polish prompt. Shared order is re-read in Mei Lin's independent context in hro_arrive_bottom, hro_reorder, hro_bulk_move and hro_undo_restores; jobs and Activity are read in independent contexts (hro_job_open, hro_activity via Aud). (3) Restart durability (Colderwater lesson 15): protocol D (functional prompt.md:59) records 'your jobs, card order per stage, notes, the last messages of your conversations, your unread count per conversation, your activity lines, and the seeded Platform Engineer order and note read in Z', calls restart_app once, signs in again and compares; hro_restart (judge.toml:413-419, w1.5) fails if anything is 'lost, reordered or duplicated' or the starting data is loaded again. These are many records produced by many revisions (multi-step moves, re-orders, undos, rejections/reopens, several conversations), not one record saved once. restart_app is a real process restart: test.sh's app-restart.sh kills the process group and relaunches node with the same DB_PATH (byte-identical to the template). The comparison is against a pre-restart baseline, so other features' defects are not deducted twice (lesson 16). Z expectations match the seed: JOB-PLAT Applied Greta Lindqvist(1), Ade Bello(2), Marco Rossi(3); Screen Priya Nair(1), Samuel Ortiz(2); APP-101 note 'Strong systems answers; weaker on incident follow-up.' Visual is read-only, polish uses its own jobs, and rewardkit runs with --max-concurrent-agent 1, so no other dimension mutates the Z baseline or races D. (4) Re-auth: the brief requires an unsent reply to survive sign-out and stay private per person; polish hro_pol_session_resume (w2) ends the session, re-signs in, checks reply and note drafts are kept and invisible to Mei Lin; hro_drafts covers reload; reload-still-signed-in is in the gate. hireops_rules.md s.6 says 'Where drafts are kept is up to you', so no server-backed draft demand is invented. Weak apps: an in-memory server passes the gate but fails hro_restart; a DB that persists cards but not position, read markers or activity fails D's order/unread/activity comparison; reseed-on-start duplicates or reset read markers fail 'not loaded again'/unread comparison; a localStorage-only board fails the independent-context gate (every binary row 0). Conforming alternative: any storage under DB_PATH and any session store pass, since D only asks for a fresh sign-in. Golden evidence (hashes verified): workspace.cjs:531-542 SIGTERMs the child, relaunches, and asserts applications, activity, job count and per-person unread equal before/after and that live updates resume; via-solve.log 'PASS restart keeps jobs, cards, order, messages, unread counts and activity without reseeding; live updates resume'. This is scripted golden evidence, not a configured judge run. Residual risk (why risk=true): (a) no full configured judge run exists (raw-evidence-index scope: 'Full configured grading/workload ... absent'), so whether the judge reaches protocol D, the last step of a very long batched functional run (timeout 9000), is unmeasured; if the budget runs out, hro_restart is NOT EXERCISED/0 even for a correct app. (b) D's post-restart readback is on the supplied page ('sign in again'), not a new independent context as the template persistence step 2 suggests ('Open a fresh browser page'). (c) The golden script does not explicitly assert notes after restart; the judge's D does compare notes.
counterexample: No passing broken app found. Closest weak case: a client that caches the board in browser storage and paints it before the server answers; D reads post-restart state in Rafael's same context, so a hasty read could see cached order. Mitigated because the gate and several Mei/Aud independent-context reads already fail a browser-only store, and unread counts, messages and activity come from the server.
suggested_fix: Optional hardening: in protocol D, after restart_app also re-read card order, notes and activity in a new independent context (e.g. as Aud), and obtain a full configured judge run confirming protocol D is reached within the functional budget.
